P.ad: Royal Palm Visitor Center, State Road 9336, Everglades National Park, FL
P.w: The park's most popular trail: a paved path and boardwalk over sawgrass marsh and Taylor Slough where alligators, turtles and anhingas gather — best in the dry-season winter.
P.k: Walk it early morning Dec–Apr; watch for vultures on car rubber.

P.w: Everglades NP's northern entrance: a 15-mile paved loop through the river of grass to a 360° observation tower — by tram tour, bicycle or on foot.

P.ad: Main Park Road, Everglades National Park, FL
P.w: A short boardwalk to a raised platform with sweeping views over the sawgrass 'river of grass'.
The park's far southern end on Florida Bay: boat tours and rentals into the backcountry, crocodiles and manatees at the marina.

P.ad: 900 N Birch Rd, Fort Lauderdale, FL
P.w: The 1920s Caribbean-plantation-style waterfront estate of artists Frederic and Evelyn Bartlett, between the Intracoastal and the beach.

P.ad: Las Olas Blvd, Fort Lauderdale, FL
P.w: Fort Lauderdale's main strolling street of restaurants, galleries and boutiques, running from downtown to the beach.

P.ad: Riverwalk, New River, Fort Lauderdale, FL
P.w: A brick promenade along the New River past mansions, the Stranahan House and riverside bars.
Built 1901 as Frank Stranahan's trading post — the oldest surviving structure in Broward County, now a museum.

P.ad: Fort Lauderdale Beach Blvd (A1A), Fort Lauderdale, FL
P.w: The former spring-break mecca, now a palm-lined promenade of white sand and turquoise water.

P.n: Miami Beach Architectural District (Art Deco Historic District)
P.ad: Ocean Drive & Collins Ave, South Beach, Miami Beach, FL
P.w: The world's largest concentration of 1920s–30s Art Deco buildings, pastel hotels along Ocean Drive — on the National Register.
P.k: Walk Ocean Drive at dusk when the neon comes on.

P.w: Design museum and library in a restored 1927 storage building — 180,000 objects on how design shaped the modern world.
Morris Lapidus' 1960 pedestrian mall — a mile of cafés, shops and people-watching.
Waterfront park and pier at the tip of South Beach watching cruise ships slide out of Government Cut.
Kenneth Treister's 1990 memorial: a 42-ft bronze arm rising from a reflecting pool, ringed by figures and a granite wall of victims' names.
Miami Beach's contemporary art museum in a 1930s Deco building in Collins Park.
Downtown's 32-acre waterfront park on Biscayne Bay, with the Noguchi-designed amphitheatre and Challenger memorial.
PAMM — Miami's flagship contemporary art museum in a Herzog & de Meuron building with hanging gardens on the bay.

P.n: Phillip and Patricia Frost Museum of Science
P.w: Science museum, planetarium and a three-level aquarium with an oculus looking up into the Gulf Stream tank.
Tony Goldman's 2009 outdoor street-art museum that turned Wynwood's warehouses into the world's mural capital.
James Deering's 1916 Italian Renaissance–style villa and formal gardens on Biscayne Bay — Miami's grandest historic estate.

P.ad: 10901 Old Cutler Rd, Coral Gables, FL
P.w: 83 acres of palms, cycads and rare tropical plants — one of the country's great tropical botanical gardens.

P.n: Biscayne National Park — Dante Fascell Visitor Center
P.w: The mainland gateway to a park that is 95% water: museum, art gallery, ranger talks, and boat trips out to the keys, reefs and Stiltsville.

P.ad: Boca Chita Key, Biscayne National Park, FL
P.w: The park's most-visited island, greeted by the ornamental lighthouse Mark Honeywell built in the 1930s.

P.ad: Biscayne Bay off Cape Florida, Biscayne National Park, FL
P.w: The six surviving stilt houses standing in the shallows of Biscayne Bay since the 1930s — seen on guided boat tours.
Big Cypress National Preserve's main visitor centre on the Tamiami Trail — alligators line the canal out front.
A boardwalk into a cypress strand that ends at a gator hole where anhingas dry their wings.
Gallery of Everglades photographer Clyde Butcher's monumental black-and-white swamp photographs; guided swamp walks.

P.ad: Loop Road (CR 94), Big Cypress National Preserve, FL
P.w: A 27-mile gravel detour off the Tamiami Trail through cypress swamp and pinelands — prime gator spotting.
The smallest post office in the United States — a 61-sq-ft former irrigation-pipe shed pressed into service after a 1953 fire.
Roadside shrine-cum-campground devoted to Florida's Bigfoot, the Skunk Ape.
Miami-Dade's 37-acre Redland botanical park of 500+ edible tropical fruits, spices and nuts — taste what's in season.
Ed Leedskalnin's single-handed carved-coral monument (1923–51), still unexplained.
Since 1933: the humans walk in cages while the primates roam free.
Florida's oldest alligator farm (1940s) at the Everglades' edge — airboat rides and gator shows.
Key Biscayne's two-mile family beach with calm water, cabanas and beachside paella.

P.n: Bill Baggs Cape Florida State Park
P.ad: 1200 S Crandon Blvd, Key Biscayne, FL
P.w: The tip of Key Biscayne: a mile of wild beach, nature trails and Miami-Dade's oldest structure, the 1825 Cape Florida Light.

P.ad: Bill Baggs Cape Florida State Park, Key Biscayne, FL
P.w: The 1825 brick lighthouse — the oldest standing structure in Miami-Dade; climb it on ranger-led tours.
Opened in 1945 as the 'colored only' beach of segregated Miami; now a historic park on Virginia Key.
Wide family beach between Bal Harbour and Sunny Isles — kite flying since 1992, a skate park, and a clothing-optional section to the north.

P.ad: Ocean Dr & Collins Ave, Miami Beach, FL
P.w: Miami's most famous sand, framed by lifeguard towers and the Art Deco skyline of Ocean Drive.
1926 Mediterranean Revival grand hotel and South Florida's only National Historic Landmark resort.

P.ad: 2701 De Soto Blvd, Coral Gables, FL
P.w: A 1924 public pool carved from a coral-rock quarry — waterfalls, grottoes and Venetian bridges; on the National Register.
Coral Gables' downtown boulevard of shops, cafés and galleries.
University of Miami's art museum, home of the Kress Collection of Renaissance and Baroque art.

P.ad: SW 8th St, Little Havana, Miami, FL
P.w: The heart of Cuban Miami: cigar rollers, ventanitas, giant painted roosters and the Walk of Fame stars for Celia Cruz and Gloria Estefan.
Shaded pavilion where the Máximo Gómez Domino Club play fierce daily games — the symbol of Little Havana.
A 1926 Art Deco cinema at Calle Ocho and 15th Ave, still screening films and hosting cultural events.

P.ad: SW 13th Ave, Little Havana, Miami, FL
P.w: A tree-lined median of monuments to Cuban history — the Eternal Torch of the Brigade 2506, the Bay of Pigs memorial.
1925 Giralda-style tower built for the Miami News; 1962–74 the Cuban Refugee Center that processed ~300,000 exiles — the 'Ellis Island of the South'. National Historic Landmark (2008).
South Florida's history museum in the Cultural Plaza; it also manages the Miami Circle.
John Eberson's 1926 atmospheric movie palace for Paramount — stars twinkle on the ceiling; a Miami Film Festival venue.
A 2,000-year-old Tequesta circle of 24 post-holes cut into limestone at the mouth of the Miami River, found in 1998. National Historic Landmark.
Overtown's 1913 theatre at the heart of 'Little Broadway', where Count Basie, Billie Holiday and Aretha Franklin played; now the Black Archives' home.

P.n: Black Police Precinct and Courthouse Museum
P.w: The 1950 precinct and courthouse where Miami's first Black officers served — now a museum of their story.

P.ad: 16711 W Dixie Hwy, North Miami Beach, FL
P.w: A 12th-century Cistercian cloister from Segovia, bought by William Randolph Hearst, shipped in crates and reassembled in North Miami Beach.

P.ad: 3400 NE 163rd St, North Miami Beach, FL
P.w: Florida's largest urban park: 1,000+ acres of mangrove estuary with kayaking, paddleboarding and 15 miles of mountain-bike trails.

P.n: Museum of Contemporary Art North Miami (MOCA)
P.w: Contemporary art museum with ~500 works and free last-Friday Jazz at MOCA concerts.
A natural limestone bridge over Arch Creek, Tequesta archaeological site and nature centre.

P.ad: 17530 W Dixie Hwy, North Miami Beach, FL
P.w: 1930s county park with a rock-built 'castle' mound, a rookery and a 1964 nine-hole course.
One of the largest private contemporary-art collections in the world (7,200+ works), in Allapattah — with two Kusama Infinity Mirror Rooms.
A 50,000-sq-ft Wynwood warehouse showing developer Martin Margulies' contemporary art and photography collection.

P.n: Institute of Contemporary Art, Miami (ICA Miami)
P.w: Free contemporary art museum in the Design District, with a sculpture garden.
The world's first museum dedicated to graffiti art, in Wynwood.
Luxury flagships threaded with serious public art and architecture — Buckminster Fuller's Fly's Eye Dome, the Le Corbusier-inspired garage.
A 2½-mile 1950s-flavoured beachfront promenade of mom-and-pop shops and ice-cream parlours, with free music at the Hollywood Beach Theatre.

P.ad: 3109 E Sunrise Blvd, Fort Lauderdale, FL
P.w: 180 acres of Old Florida hammock and mangrove between the ocean and the Intracoastal — paddling, trails, picnic lawns.
200+ hands-on exhibits, live-animal habitats and a five-storey IMAX on the Riverwalk.
60-acre botanical garden and wildlife sanctuary with some of Florida's largest, oldest trees and a 1930s house museum.

P.ad: 3600 W Sample Rd, Coconut Creek, FL
P.w: The 'Butterfly Capital of the World': 20,000 butterflies and birds in screened aviaries and gardens.
The only subtropical zoo in the continental US — 2,000+ animals in open, moated habitats.
Charles Deering's 1920s bayfront estate with what's believed to be the largest old-growth coastal tropical hardwood hammock in the continental US — nature walks, boat trips, night hikes.

P.ad: 9610 Old Cutler Rd, Coral Gables, FL
P.w: County park whose man-made atoll pool is refreshed by Biscayne Bay's tides.
Bayside county park and marina next to Biscayne NP's visitor centre, on land donated in 1938.
N.B.T. Roney's 1925 'historic Spanish village' — two pink-stucco, tile-roofed blocks of cafés under striped awnings.

P.ad: 2000 Convention Center Dr, Miami Beach, FL
P.w: 4.5 acres of orchids, a Japanese garden and a living wall beside the Convention Center — free.
Florida Jewish history since 1763, housed in two restored former synagogues in South of Fifth.
Plant explorer David Fairchild's nine-acre Coconut Grove estate, now a National Tropical Botanical Garden; tours by reservation.
The 1891 home of Commodore Ralph Munroe — the oldest house in Miami still on its original site, on a waterfront lawn that hosts bluegrass and folk nights.
Coconut Grove's renovated open-air shopping and dining centre.
Virginia Key's marine park (1955) permanently closed on 12 October 2025 after 70 years; a replacement aquarium is planned for ~2030.
1925 racetrack on the National Register — 200 acres of royal palms, a casino, quarter-horse racing and its famous Audubon-sanctuary colony of pink flamingos.
Glenn Curtiss's 1926 Arabian Nights city: the domed, minaretted Moorish Revival city hall is the starting point for a tour of ~90 Moorish buildings.

P.ad: 347 Don Shula Dr, Miami Gardens, FL
P.w: Home of the Miami Dolphins and the Hurricanes; Super Bowl LIV and the Miami Grand Prix circuit.

F.w: Miami's only two-Michelin-star restaurant (2026 Florida guide): Robuchon's counter-dining format in the Design District.
One Michelin star (2026) — Coral Gables omakase counter.
One Michelin star (2026): chef Michael Beltran's Coconut Grove flagship, Miami-Cuban flavours in fine-dining form.
One Michelin star (2026): the strip-mall Italian in Little River that became one of Miami's hardest reservations.
One Michelin star (2026): the Miami outpost of the New York Korean steakhouse.
One Michelin star (2026): chef Juan Manuel Barrientos' Colombian tasting menu on the Miami River in Brickell.
One Michelin star (2026): an eight-seat omakase hidden behind a Wynwood taco counter.
F.k: Order: Omakase behind a taco shop

F.w: One Michelin star (2026): garden-led French dining in the Design District.
One Michelin star (2026): heirloom-corn Mexican cooking in Coconut Grove.
One Michelin star (2026) — the first kosher restaurant in the world to earn a Michelin star.
One Michelin star (2026): a serene Japanese omakase in Little River.
One Michelin star (2026): Top Chef winner Jeremy Ford's South of Fifth tasting room.
F.k: Order: Chef Jeremy Ford's tasting menu

F.w: One Michelin star (2026): German star chef Tristan Brandt's tasting room inside the Carillon on North Beach.
One Michelin star (2026): Thomas Keller's mid-century continental dining room in the restored 1930 Surf Club.
Michelin Bib Gourmand — heads Miami's Bib list; Vietnamese cooking in a tiny downtown room.
F.k: Order: Phở and Vietnamese home cooking

F.w: Michelin Bib Gourmand: pastry chef Antonio Bachour's all-day bakery-café.
F.k: Order: Pastry-chef plated desserts and croissants

F.ad: 3444 Main Hwy, Coconut Grove, Miami, FL
F.w: Michelin Bib Gourmand Cuban diner from Ariete's Michael Beltran & Monika Dominguez; its short-rib croqueta inspired the Infatuation's unique-croquetas guide.
F.k: Order: Pan con lechón, short-rib croqueta, Cuban diner breakfast

F.w: Michelin Bib Gourmand Turkish restaurant.
Michelin Bib Gourmand: chef Niven Patel's Indian kitchen cooking with produce from his own Homestead farm.
Michelin Bib Gourmand: the Brooklyn barbecue institution's Miami pit in Allapattah.
Michelin Bib Gourmand neighbourhood restaurant in Little River.
Michelin Bib Gourmand: the Miami Beach branch of Brooklyn's famous Carroll Gardens pizzeria.
Michelin Bib Gourmand: Greek-Turkish cooking in a whitewashed 1940s house and garden.
F.k: Order: Aegean mezze in a cottage garden

F.w: Michelin Bib Gourmand: James Beard winner Michael Schwartz's Design District pioneer (2007).
Michelin Bib Gourmand Viet-Cajun spot on Biscayne Boulevard.
Michelin Bib Gourmand and New Times' Best Cuban Sandwich 2024 — the modern standard-bearer for the Cubano on Calle Ocho.
F.k: Order: The Cubano — week-marinated pork, house-brined ham, house bread

F.ad: 396 Alhambra Cir Ste 155, Coral Gables, FL
F.w: Michelin Bib Gourmand dim-sum-and-noodles spot from chef Pablo Zitzmann.

F.ad: 1315 Ponce de Leon Blvd, Coral Gables, FL
F.w: Michelin Bib Gourmand café.

F.ad: 17034 W Dixie Hwy, North Miami Beach, FL
F.w: New Michelin Bib Gourmand 2026: tiny counter-service Peruvian seafood bar in a North Miami Beach strip mall.
New Michelin Bib Gourmand 2026: chef Alejandra Espinoza's Ecuadorian cooking.
New Michelin Bib Gourmand 2026: creative Chinese classics in a dim Upper East Side room.
F.k: Order: Crispy crab-leg rangoon, Hennessy orange chicken

F.w: Little Havana's landmark since 1971 — New Times calls its ventanita 'ground zero for coffee culture in Miami'; Michelin-recommended.
F.k: Order: Cafecito at the ventanita, croquetas, Cuban sandwich

F.ad: 4612 S Le Jeune Rd, Coral Gables, FL
F.w: Coral Gables Cuban institution since 1995; New Times' best Cuban sandwiches and Michelin's best Cuban restaurants list (2024).
Ortelio 'El Mago' Cárdenas' frita counter — New Times' best frita cubana, Eater 38 'best fritas in Miami', and where President Obama ordered fritas in 2010.
Miami Beach's oldest restaurant (1913) and the home of stone crab; open mid-October to mid-May for the season. Eater 38 'original Miami Beach power lunch'.
F.k: Order: Stone crab claws with mustard sauce, key lime pie

F.w: Little Haiti griot specialist — crunchy fried pork with pikliz, huge plates for under $10.
Wilkinson 'Ken' Sejour's Haitian-Bahamian seafood counter — 'if you want to talk Haitian food, you start at Chef Creole'; Anthony Bourdain filmed here for No Reservations.
F.k: Order: Griot, conch salad, fried snapper

F.w: Chef Juan Chipoco's downtown Peruvian — New Times Best Ceviche 2024; on Infatuation and Time Out's Peruvian lists.
F.k: Order: Ceviche in leche de tigre or rocoto

F.ad: 525 N Fort Lauderdale Beach Blvd, Fort Lauderdale, FL
F.w: Fort Lauderdale's Michelin star (2026): chef Ryan Ratino's counter at MAASS in the Four Seasons.
Maria Teresa Gallina & Nicolas Martinez: James Beard Best Chef: South semifinalists 2026.
Michael Schwartz's bayfront Latin restaurant in Edgewater — James Beard 2026 semifinalist for Outstanding Wine & Beverages.
F.k: Order: Wood-fired Latin seafood on the bay

F.w: James Beard 2026 semifinalist, Best New Bar.
Michelin Bib Gourmand (2025, retained 2026): chef Rino Cerbone's Italian.

F.ad: 620 S Federal Hwy, Fort Lauderdale, FL
F.w: Michelin-recommended (2026): chef Daniel Ganem's Florida-sourced steakhouse.

F.ad: 525 N Fort Lauderdale Beach Blvd, Fort Lauderdale, FL
F.w: Michelin-recommended (2026) Eastern Mediterranean at the Four Seasons, chef Brandon Salomon.

F.ad: 6234 N Federal Hwy, Fort Lauderdale, FL
F.w: Michelin-recommended (2026); the Infatuation calls it the best Thai restaurant in South Florida.
The Redland's famous fruit stand, run by Robert Moehling since he was six (1960): lychees, sapotes, carambolas — and milkshakes in every flavour — on the road to the Everglades.
F.k: Order: Fresh tropical-fruit milkshake (mamey, key lime, guanabana)

F.w: Wine made from subtropical fruit — lychee, carambola, avocado — on tropical grounds with weekend live music.
F.k: Order: Lychee and carambola fruit wines

F.w: Pan cubano baker for 40+ years; Infatuation rates its pastelitos among the county's best and New Times lists it in Miami's ten best.
Family-run old-school Cuban lunch counter holding out amid Edgewater/Wynwood's towers — sandwiches stuffed with croquetas.
F.k: Order: Cubano preparado con croquetas, Cuban breakfast

F.w: Croqueta king since 1977 — the Infatuation's pick for Miami's best croquetas, and 'the most Miami drive-thru'.
Versailles' sister restaurant since the 1970s ('the food is actually better here'); its ventanitas are fixtures across the county.
F.k: Order: Home-style Cuban plates, ventanita cafecito

F.w: Flagami's Cuban café's Brickell outpost — a true ventanita, under-the-radar croquetas and a New Times top-100 Cuban sandwich.
F.k: Order: Cuban sandwich, croquetas, ventanita cafecito

F.w: Cantinero Julio Cabrera's Havana-style cocktail bar with JBF-winner Michelle Bernstein's kitchen and live trova — recognised by the Florida Michelin Guide.
F.k: Order: Julio Cabrera's daiquiris, Michelle Bernstein's ropa vieja

F.w: Classic Little Haiti spot with a lush courtyard of hammocks and roosters; some of Miami's best Haitian food.
F.k: Order: Oxtail, fried snapper — in a garden courtyard

F.w: An essential Little Haiti stop for Haitian home cooking.
F.k: Order: Griot, legim, diri djon djon

F.w: Eater 38: 'the pan con lechón is arguably the best in town' — crackling-studded roast pork on Cuban bread.
Tamiami Trail swamp-food stand since the early 1960s, beside the Original Air Boat Tour (1945) — frog legs and gator tail straight from the Glades.
F.k: Order: Frog legs and gator tail, cornmeal-fried

F.w: Everglades City waterfront fish house famous for stone crab claws landed by its own boats.
F.k: Order: Stone crab claws off its own boats, gator bites

F.w: Tin-roofed Tamiami Trail café in Ochopee serving catfish, frog legs, gator and blue crab.
F.k: Order: Frog legs, soft-shell crab, gator

F.w: New Michelin-recommended (2026) omakase counter in Coral Gables.
Michelin-recommended (2025) in the MiMo neighbourhood.
Chef Nando Chang's ten-seat Nikkei counter — Michelin star in 2025; Itamae began as a Bib Gourmand stall.
Michelin-recommended (2025) near Little Havana.
Michelin-recommended (2025) seafood restaurant in Coconut Grove.

F.ad: Julia & Henry's, 200 E Flagler St, Miami, FL
F.w: Michelin-recommended (2025) Italian inside the Julia & Henry's food hall downtown.
Michelin-recommended (2025): contemporary menu with Japanese influences.
Michelin-recommended (2025) Little River steakhouse in an Old Florida garden setting.
Michelin-recommended (2025) Neapolitan pizza in an intimate downtown room; its burger is on New Times' best-burgers list.
F.k: Order: Neapolitan pizza; the much-talked-about burger

F.w: Zak Stern's Wynwood sourdough bakery — a Michelin Bib Gourmand in the inaugural 2022 Florida guide.
Tiny, cash-and-queue Thai tapas counter — Michelin Bib Gourmand (2022).
F.k: Order: Thai tapas (khao soi, crispy pork)

F.w: Marcus Samuelsson's Overtown outpost of Harlem's Red Rooster — Michelin Bib Gourmand (2022).
F.k: Order: Fried yardbird, Overtown soul food

F.w: Aegean meze house in Wynwood — Michelin Bib Gourmand (2022).
F.k: Order: Aegean meze from the wood grill

F.ad: The Stanton South Beach, 161 Ocean Dr, Miami Beach, FL
F.w: Hidden omakase room inside Sushi Azabu (Greystone Hotel) — one Michelin star in the inaugural 2022 guide.
Michael Beltran's French-meets-Miami brasserie in Miami Worldcenter — Michelin-recommended (2023).

F.ad: 1500 San Ignacio Ave, Coral Gables, FL
F.w: Lavish Coral Gables Italian from the team behind Michelin-starred Fiola D.C. — Michelin-recommended (2023).
The Four Seasons Surf Club's champagne-bar terrace restaurant — Michelin-recommended (2023).
F.k: Order: Coastal Italian on the terrace

F.ad: 804 Ponce de Leon Blvd, Coral Gables, FL
F.w: Chef Michael Bolen's contemporary American in the former Eating House space — Michelin-recommended (2023).
Some of Miami's best barbecue, smoked in a rundown caddie shack on Kendall's Killian Greens golf course — New Times readers' Best Barbecue 2025.
F.k: Order: Brisket and burnt ends from a golf-course shack

F.w: West Kendall pit fusing Miami's Latin staples with American barbecue — on the Infatuation's Kendall guide and New Times' ten best barbecue.
Cuban bakery chain whose original on US-1 in Pinecrest is the most consistent (Infatuation) — New Times readers' Best Bakery 2025.
Porthole-doored, no-frills raw bar on the Intracoastal, unchanged since the 1970s — a Fort Lauderdale locals' legend for half a century.
F.k: Order: Peel-and-eat shrimp, raw oysters and clams

F.ad: 250 W State Road 84, Fort Lauderdale, FL
F.w: Open 24/7 since 1967–68 — a neon-lit 'retro since it was new' roadside greasy spoon with enormous plates.
F.k: Order: 24-hour diner breakfast under the neon
